key_insight: A two-dimensional chiral fluid has a genuine antisymmetric pressure contribution that comes from a parity-breaking pseudo-scalar, not from the usual kinetic or collisional pressure channels.
engineering_relevance: This implies continuum and surrogate fluid models for chiral or micropolar media must include rotational viscosity and chiral pressure even in homogeneous, zero-gradient regimes.
method: Derive the microscopic expression for the antisymmetric pressure contribution.
Connect the chiral pressure to the rotational (vortex) viscosity of micropolar hydrodynamics.
Compute the kinetic rotational viscosity for rough disks to Gaussian order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytic microscopic derivation, along with a computed kinetic value for rough disks and the existence of a steady homogeneous Quiescent Chiral State.
watch_item: Standard distribution-function expansions may be incomplete unless they explicitly include the non-vanishing pseudo-scalar variable present in chiral fluids.
paper_title: Microscopic origin of the chiral pressure in a two-dimensional fluid
